transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-12 15:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Michael (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Daniel (Ridgeback ML), Priya (Ridgeback Platform), Evelyn (Ridgeback CTO), Samir (Ridgeback SRE)

Summary: quick sync; run through bench numbers; decide on isolation tests and pricing ask. Shared bench sheet: https://redwood.app/bench/ridgeback-2026-11-12

00:00:05 Michael (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: run through the latest bench results we posted yesterday, triage the tail latency for large concurrent runs, and agree next steps for the dedicated slot request.
00:00:18 Daniel (Dir. ML Eng): thanks mike. we looked through the sheet, um, initial reaction is the median numbers look good but the 95/99 spikes are concerning. our incumbent, IncumbentModelCo, has smoother tails at the same qps.
00:00:33 Sofia (SE): yeah so to clarify — our median at 512 tok is about 48 ms p99 is 420 ms when we do a 200 qps concurrency burst, so there's a clear tail. that's with prefix cache active and quantization q4f16.
00:00:50 Priya (Platform): can you remind us which model variant you used in that run? we might have misread the sheet.
00:00:56 Michael: sure — that was redwood-model-1.1-quant4 (approx). i think the sheet label said rwd-1.1-q4. there may be a small mismatch with the model the incumbent uses, but we tried to keep prompt shapes identical.
00:01:12 Evelyn (CTO): importance here is predictable 95th latency under load; our SLAs to customers are tight. cost matters but predictability is higher priority.
00:01:25 Jordan (CSM): noted — the ask last week was pricing for a dedicated slot to stabilize performance as well as a routing policy to fall back to a lower-cost variant.
00:01:38 Daniel: exactly. also want to understand if the p99 spikes are KV cache warmup or something like kernel scheduling.
00:01:47 Sofia: good point. we suspect KV cache fragmentation under multi-tenant bursts — when you have concurrent large context reuse sometimes the cache eviction pattern creates tail latency. to prove that, we can run the same load with KV cache disabled, so every request is cold on kv. if the tail improves or worsens that tells us something.
00:02:05 Samir (SRE): quick question — how do you measure tail? is this across pods or within a single serving instance?
00:02:12 Sofia: it's aggregated across the serving pool; the bench sheet has a breakdown per instance but the p99 reported is cluster-level. i'll attach the per-pod trace.
00:02:20 Daniel: ok can we also get a flame graph or timeline? those help us see if it's GC-like stalls or kernel scheduling.
00:02:28 Sofia: we'll include traces — note the runtime uses a continuous-batching optimizer and we've seen small stalls when batch size spikes; that might look like a GC pause but it's actually the batching boundary.
00:02:42 Michael: to be explicit on delta vs incumbent: median is ~15% better on redwood for our config, unit cost about 10% lower. the p99 is the delta that matters to ridgeback.
00:02:55 Evelyn: yeah, median is great but the customer impact is p99.
00:03:03 Priya: question on quantization — did you try q3a? we're trying to balance latency and quality.
00:03:10 Sofia: we did run q3a briefly; it helped reduce median by ~8 ms but increased p99 variance slightly. q4f16 seems the best balance currently. we can re-run with q3a at your payloads.
00:03:22 Daniel: would be helpful. also, when you say "increased p99 variance" can you share the distribution? a histogram would be perfect.
00:03:30 Sofia: sure — the sheet has histograms per run, i'll link them in the notes.
00:03:36 Michael: ok next, dedicated slot pricing — Jordan, can you summarize what we can offer?
00:03:41 Jordan: yes; for a reserved dedicated pool sized for your 200 qps steady state we have two options: monthly reserved with burst buffer or annual at a discount plus 99.9% SLA. the price delta vs hosted varies — i'll send an exact quote; ballpark monthly is three to four X per-hosted unit but you get predictable tail performance.
00:04:02 Evelyn: three to four X is a lot. can you give a simple example vs our current bill from IncumbentModelCo?
00:04:10 Michael: it'll vary by token mix; we modeled 20M tokens/day and put some numbers in the sheet (see pricing tab). net savings per token vs incumbent on median usage is roughly 12% but you get stronger SLOs.
00:04:25 Daniel: okay, for us the math is: if dedicated reduces p99 by half, that gives us less retries and lower effective cost. so we need the proof point.
00:04:35 Sofia: proof point — we can spin a dedicated slot as a short pilot (7 days) and run your payloads under your traffic shape. that will show real p99 deltas.
00:04:46 Priya: what about network egress for private/vpc tests? our infra team will need a checklist.
00:04:52 Samir: yes we have firewall rules and egress constraints, need explicit ports and egress CIDRs.
00:04:58 Jordan: we'll provide the on-prem/vpc checklist. i'll follow up with the exact firewall/ports and sample terraform if helpful.
00:05:07 Michael: back to the bench: we saw the largest tail spikes when we increased sequence length to 1k tokens and concurrently ran 150 qps. at 256 tokens the p99 is much closer to median.
00:05:22 Daniel: that's consistent with our observations — longer contexts amplify cache pressure.
00:05:26 Sofia: right, two experiments to isolate: 1) disable KV cache; 2) reduce batch horizon to force smaller continuous batches. we'll run both and compare.
00:05:37 Michael: and please capture the 95/99 and per-pod traces.
00:05:40 Daniel: got it.
00:05:42 Priya: do you have a simple routing fallback playbook — like if p99 > 400ms, route to smaller model? we need deterministic rules.
00:05:50 Sofia: yes we have routing policy templates; we can propose a rule: primary route to rwd-1.1-q4, fallback to rwd-0.9-small with lower context and lower cost; also an automatic ramp-down throttle if burst rate exceeds threshold.
00:06:05 Evelyn: can that be done without changing our client code?
00:06:08 Michael: yes — routing is at the platform side; you interact with the same API and we handle variant switching. we log all fallbacks.
00:06:16 Daniel: ok good. for audit reasons we also need full request/response hashes logged — we can't store PII but need request IDs.
00:06:24 Jordan: we can provide obfuscated request IDs and flow-level traces; for private deployments we can also integrate with your KMS and audit logs.
00:06:33 Samir: about KMS — we're evaluating HSM for keys; is Redwood compatible?
00:06:39 Michael: yes — we have KMS integrations and an HSM path for private; our security docs are in the repo, i'll share SSO/SAML and SOC2 artifacts after this call.
00:06:50 Evelyn: great. anything else from the bench that surprised you?
00:06:54 Sofia: one oddity: we saw a small number of requests that timed out and retried ended up inflating p99; so part of tail is client-side retries stacking. would be good to instrument client-side retry timing too.
00:07:08 Daniel: we can add that instrumentation.
00:07:10 Michael: wrapping up — agreed next steps: Sofia runs two isolation experiments (KV off and smaller batch horizon) and uploads traces; Michael to produce dedicated slot proposal and pricing; Jordan provides on-prem checklist and SSO/KMS doc links; Ridgeback to send SLOs and payloads.
00:07:30 Priya: can we add a short 30-minute follow-up after experiments?
00:07:35 Michael: yes let's tentatively schedule for next Tuesday same time.
00:07:38 Evelyn: works for me.

-- End of main transcript (rest is Q&A and small clarifications) --

30:12:05 Daniel: slight note — one of the histograms in the sheet labels the baseline incorrectly as CloudAI. can you correct that?
30:12:12 Sofia: ah thanks, we'll fix that label; some of the auto-exports swapped names.
30:12:18 Samir: also will need the specific port list earlier.
30:12:24 Jordan: yes will send checklist and a short terraform snippet.

Crosstalk / filler: (laughs) um, yeah, mm-hmm, okay, cool.

References shared: bench sheet, pricing tab, security deck: https://redwood.app/bench/ridgeback-2026-11-12 | https://redwood.app/security/soc2 | pricing draft in CRM-78421 notes.

Action items recap: Michael to send pricing & slot, Sofia to run KV-off + batch-horizon runs and upload traces, Daniel to send SLOs & payloads.

End meeting.
